{"decision":"🔄 **WIDENED 2026-08-14 to ALL TWENTY SERVED SKILLS** by `dec:idea-does-every-served-skill-get-a-command` (accepted, option A). The exception below still stands exactly as reasoned — skills, working instructions and everything else remain SERVED, and only commands are installed — but the SET is no longer eight. **Twenty-two command files now ship** (twenty fronting a skill, plus `debt.md` and `decisions.md` which front tools), and `skill_lint` now fails a skill that no command names, so the number cannot silently fall behind again. The original ruling, and its reasoning, is kept below unedited.

════════ AS RULED 2026-07-28 ════════

The eight slash commands (`/gaps`, `/health`, `/where`, `/req`, `/decisions`, `/debt`, `/brainstorm`, `/kpp`) are INSTALLED into a consumer project's `.claude/commands/`. Skills, working instructions and everything else remain SERVED. Anthony's call, 2026-07-28.","name":"Slash commands ship with the kit — the one narrow exception to serving everything","rationale":"QUALIFIES `dec:skills-served` rather than overturning it, and the distinction is what makes the exception safe.

WHY THAT DECISION EXISTS: a copied skill goes stale, and the agent then loads last release's content in preference to what the server would serve. That happened here for four releases running without anything noticing, which is why nothing is copied.

WHY A COMMAND IS DIFFERENT: each is four lines that name a skill and say how to report the answer. There is no version-coupled content in it. When the skill behind it changes, the command is still correct, because the skill is fetched fresh at use time — the command is a pointer, and the thing it points at is the thing that moves.

THE ONE WAY IT CAN ROT, and it is now closed: a command could name a skill that no longer exists. `skill_lint` fails on exactly that, so the failure is caught in this repo rather than discovered in a consumer's, where the symptom would be an agent reporting it cannot find a skill the user was told to use. The mirror is byte-checked too, so `.claude/commands` cannot drift from the kit source.

WHAT IT COSTS IF WE ARE WRONG: eight small files in a consumer repo, each independently deletable, none of which changes behaviour when stale. Compare the cost of a stale skill, which silently answers with last release's method.

WHY IT WAS WORTH DOING AT ALL: without them a consumer install is experienced as BROKEN rather than thin — the skills are reachable and nothing tells you they are. That is the same invisibility `req:kit-reaches-the-agent` was raised for, one layer up: the pointer now reaches the agent, and the commands are what make the reachable thing usable.","status":"accepted"}
